facts: The timeline splits a sound wherever its pitch moves (beyond 2% or 5 Hz between tenths of a second), so sweeps, melodies, vibrato and beeps became short pieces.

Now a run of short pieces, across silences of a tenth of a second or less, counts as one sound once together it lasts longer than ignore_ms; it keeps a pitch only if every piece is within 5% of one.

facts: Stop the daemon first, then simulators, then emulators, then adb.

The daemon goes first because it owns the device-side sessions: killing a device under a live session leaves instrumentation running against hardware about to vanish, and an emulator coming back with the same serial meets a dead cached session.
docs/checks/clean-stop.sh --quit does it in that order, and waits for the daemon to exit before stopping any device.

facts: No. On Windows Mobium drives Android only; iOS is not possible there.
Mobium drives iOS through xcrun simctl and WebDriverAgent, and a real iPhone needs WebDriverAgent built and signed by xcodebuild and reached over CoreDevice's tunnel — all of which are macOS-only.
Nor through another machine: --remote, which drives a Mac's devices over SSH, needs a Unix socket on the caller's side and refuses on Windows.

What Flutter does not publish, Mobium cannot see: a CustomPaint widget with no Semantics, a game's canvas, an icon with no label (it maps as a bare Button).
